full_judgment: 13. Mr. A.M. Amin uddin, learned Attorney General with Mr. Sk. Md. Morshed, learned Additional Attorney General, Mr. Mehedi Hesan Chowdhury, learned Additional Attorney General and Mr. Mohammad Saiful Alam, learned Assistant Attorney General appearing on behalf of respondent No.1 supporting the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division, submits that earlier the accused-petitioners challenged the instant proceeding of the case after taking cognizance of the offence in Criminal Miscellaneous Case Nos.49766 of 2021 and 49112 of 2021 in the High Court Division and ultimately the rules issued in those two criminal miscellaneous cases were discharged and then they unsuccessfully moved to this Division in Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos.1077 and 1078 of 2022. Again the accused-petitioners have challenged the proceedings of the case after framing charges under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashment of the same on identical grounds, which is not remissible in the eye of law. He submits that the subsequent action of challenging the proceeding at the stage of framing charges against the accused-petitioners is tantamount to review the earlier judgment and order passed by the High Court Division which has been affirmed by this Division-which-is not permissible in law. However, he submits that there is no scope for raising question of res-judicata in the instant case because the instant case has been initiated for continuous breach of the provisions of Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006 which is criminal offence. Referring to the Notification dated 24.01.2017 learned Attorney General also submits that the same is a public document having been published in the Gazette Notification which enjoys a presumption as to regularity as per provision of section 114, Illustration (e) of the Evidence Act, 1872 and contents of the document itself shows that the complainant has been authorized to lodge the petition of complaint so the submissions of the learned Advocate for the accused-petitioners that the complainant has no locus standi to lodge the complaint before the Labour Court does not have any leg to stmt. Lastly, he submits that the Labour Court did not commit any illegality in finding charges against the accused-petkioners, and, thus, the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division does not call for any interference by this Division.
